subject: exfat: speed-up dir read-ahead.
author: Sorgelig

upstream.vanilla_file_line: NOT PRESENT AT THIS SITE. fs/exfat/dir.c:659-680 in linux-6.18.y at the release commit 1c732c6b94f0faee1526bd375add2fe10cba2e26 ("Linux 6.18.49") has exfat_dir_readahead() with the bare sb_breadahead() loop the fork commit wraps -- unmodified, no plug. At torvalds/linux v7.3-rc2 tip (50d05c7c76c9, depth-1 clone, grafted -- no history available for this file) `grep -rn exfat_dir_readahead fs/exfat/` and `grep -rn blk_start_plug fs/exfat/dir.c` both return ZERO matches: the function itself does not exist in mainline dir.c any more. Directory dentry read-ahead was refactored into exfat_get_dentry() (fs/exfat/dir.c, mainline lines ~648-663), which calls a new shared helper exfat_blk_readahead(sb, sec, &ra, &cnt, end) defined in fs/exfat/fatent.c:159-183 -- that helper (not exfat_dir_readahead) is what wraps sb_breadahead() in blk_start_plug/blk_finish_plug (fatent.c:180,182). v7.2.3 (linux-7.2.y head 58e7295cfecaddec94629160386412e0f2b1e8fe) already carries this exact mainline shape: fs/exfat/dir.c has no exfat_dir_readahead and no blk_start_plug at all; exfat_get_dentry() at v7.2.3 dir.c:630-663 calls exfat_blk_readahead() at line 657, and fatent.c:159-183 (v7.2.3) is byte-identical in structure to mainline's fatent.c, plug included.

provenance_doc_ref: none -- this commit postdates docs/patch-provenance.md's baseline by five years and is not covered there.

impact.effect_if_absent: Directory listing on an exFAT-formatted data partition issues its sb_breadahead() block reads one at a time instead of as a single batched I/O plug. Nothing errors or misbehaves -- exfat_dir_readahead() still reads exactly the same sectors in the same order -- but each sb_breadahead() call is dispatched and unplugged individually instead of being merged into one request at blk_finish_plug() time, so directory scans over large clusters (exactly the MiSTer file browser's workload: a games folder with hundreds/thousands of entries) issue more, smaller I/O requests and take measurably longer to become responsive, especially on removable/USB exFAT media where per-request latency dominates.
affected_hardware: exFAT-formatted MiSTer data partition/USB storage, any device -- this is a block-layer scheduling change, not device-specific

forward_port.effort: trivial -- 4-line hunk (one #include, a struct blk_plug plug; declaration, blk_start_plug/blk_finish_plug bracketing the existing for-loop), verified to apply at `patch -p1 -F0` with zero fuzz/offset against 6.18.49's fs/exfat/dir.c (dry-run in /tmp/q6work/apply-618). Does NOT apply to v7.2.3's fs/exfat/dir.c at any fuzz: `patch -p1 -F0 --dry-run` reports 'Hunk #1 FAILED at 6. Hunk #2 FAILED at 644. 2 out of 2 hunks FAILED' because v7.2.3 has no exfat_dir_readahead() function and no bare sb_breadahead() loop to wrap -- 7.x's directory read-ahead was already rewritten (exfat_get_dentry + exfat_blk_readahead, matching mainline) before this fork commit existed, so the fork's plug is functionally already present there under a different name/shape. Do not port 0050 into linux-patches-beta/.

notes:
HYPOTHESIS REFUTED ON THE 'IS IT IN MAINLINE' AXIS, BUT NOT ON THE FORM IT PREDICTED. PLAN.md 2.6 poses a binary: mainline has the same plug -> 0047-pattern mainline-attributed backport; mainline doesn't -> fork code with Erra's authorship. The actual mainline state does not fit the binary cleanly: mainline DOES achieve the same effect (plugged directory-entry read-ahead) but via a completely different, larger refactor (exfat_get_dentry()+exfat_blk_readahead(), shared with the FAT-chain read-ahead in fatent.c) that replaced exfat_dir_readahead() entirely -- there is no mainline commit that adds 'blk_start_plug/blk_finish_plug around exfat_dir_readahead's sb_breadahead loop' because that function no longer exists upstream. Backporting '0047-style' would mean either (a) porting the whole exfat directory-access rewrite (far beyond this item's scope and a poor match for a MiSTer-specific 6.18.y base), or (b) claiming mainline authorship for a hunk mainline never actually wrote in this shape, which would be false attribution. The correct call under the plan's own fallback is therefore the SECOND branch: carry as fork code, crediting Giancarlo Erra (PR #88, 97887b3413) as the real author, and record Sorgelig's re-commit (9854075c8) as the fork-branch delivery vehicle. Because mainline cannot be cited as the SOURCE of this exact hunk (equivalence is graded 'partial': same technique, same cited precedent -- 'matching the allocation-bitmap implementation' -- different code entirely), this is NOT a 0047-pattern record despite superficially resembling one.

ALLOCATION-BITMAP PRECEDENT, QUOTED. The commit message says the change matches 'the allocation-bitmap implementation.' In 6.18.49 fs/exfat/balloc.c:73-118 (exfat_allocate_bitmap), the precedent is: `struct blk_plug plug;` at line 77, then inside the sector-loading loop: `if (max_ra_count && 0 == (i % max_ra_count)) { blk_start_plug(&plug); for (j = i; j < min(max_ra_count, sbi->map_sectors - i) + i; j++) sb_breadahead(sb, sector + j); blk_finish_plug(&plug); }` (balloc.c:109-114) -- immediately followed by `sbi->vol_amap[i] = sb_bread(sb, sector + i);`. This precedent still exists verbatim in our 6.18.49 checkout; the fork commit's four lines are a faithful, minimal copy of that pattern applied to the sibling function exfat_dir_readahead(). Note mainline's balloc.c has itself moved to calling the shared exfat_blk_readahead() helper (balloc.c:106-107 in mainline calls it directly) rather than an inline blk_start_plug -- i.e. mainline generalized the SAME precedent this fork commit is imitating, just one refactor step further, and did so for both balloc.c and dir.c at once. This strengthens rather than weakens the case that the fork's direction is correct; mainline simply got there via a bigger rewrite.

STABLE-RANGE CHECK. `git -C $S/linux log --oneline v6.18.39..HEAD -- fs/exfat/` (HEAD = 6.18.49 release commit 1c732c6b94f0) returns exactly one commit: 62dde71ca2c8 'exfat: preserve benign secondary entries during rename and move' (Rochan Avlur, upstream 942296784b2a, Cc: stable). Its dir.c hunk touches exfat_init_ext_entry() and exfat_free_benign_secondary_clusters()-adjacent code (diff context starting at mainline-relative line ~481, function signature change to exfat_init_ext_entry), nowhere near exfat_dir_readahead() (line 659 in 6.18.49) -- disjoint, confirmed by reading the diff. `git log -G'blk_start_plug' v6.18.39..HEAD -- fs/exfat/` returns nothing: no stable point release in our pinned range touched plug usage in exFAT. So there is no by-tag 'absent from 6.18.y' story to tell for a mainline SHA (unlike 0047/6332499e7) -- there is no mainline SHA to be absent, which is exactly why this is fork-authored code, not a missing-backport.

0031 COLLISION -- CONFIRMED DISJOINT, EMPIRICALLY. 0031-exfat-samsung-symlinks.patch's fs/exfat/dir.c hunks are at `@@ -268,8 +268,10 @@ get_new:` (dir_emit/DT_LNK classifier) and `@@ -396,6 +398,10 @@ static void exfat_set_entry_type` (TYPE_SYMLINK case) -- both far from line 659's exfat_dir_readahead and from the top-of-file #include block (0031 never touches includes in dir.c). Applied 0031 then the fork's hunk sequentially to a fresh copy of 6.18.49's fs/exfat/dir.c in /tmp/q6work/combo: `patch -p1 -F0` succeeded for 0031 (one hunk offset +1 line elsewhere, unrelated file), then the fork hunk applied with hunk #2 landing at an offset (+44 lines, from 0031's earlier insertions) but ZERO fuzz -- confirmed exfat_dir_readahead/blk_start_plug/blk_finish_plug all present correctly in the combined result. Order (0031 before 0050) is required for the observed offset to resolve; 0050 should be numbered/ordered after 0031 in the series file, consistent with the existing 00xx numbering being roughly chronological.

WHY equivalence=partial NOT byte-identical/equivalent. 'equivalent' would claim mainline's code path produces the identical dispatch pattern for the identical call; it does not exercise the same call graph (exfat_dir_readahead is gone, folded into exfat_get_dentry with a sliding ra/ra_cnt window across multiple dentry-set reads, not a single fixed-radius readahead per exfat_dir_readahead call) -- 'contradicted' would be wrong too, since the effect (plugged batch readahead beating the allocation-bitmap precedent) is not opposed, just achieved differently at a different abstraction level. 'partial' is the accurate grade.
